unlabeled_first_impression: A huge black steam locomotive overwhelms a sunlit domestic room. A woman holds a small matchbox from which a curving string of much smaller railway carriages runs toward the large engine. The shared light and ordinary room make this size relationship feel tangible and strange.

calibration.basis: The scale paradox is the image main read before the figure or room; this is a perceptual observation, not a count of odd props or prompt sentences.

testcase_results.evidence: At thumbnail and native scales, the huge boiler and matchbox-to-train curve form the governing visual hierarchy.

Small passenger carriages emerge from the box toward a large locomotive. The same locomotive boiler and wheels are not visibly continuous across both scales, and both rails cannot be traced together through the cardboard lip and down to the floor. A general train connection does not satisfy one locomotive and same two rails.

At native contact crop, one palm supports the tray and the other fingers hold the sleeve, while the small railway vehicles cross the opening with cardboard edges in front. This passes the separately observed human support and box-passage boundary only; it does not imply the complete two-rail route.

The generated face is guided by the portrait with a dark chin-length bob, wispy bangs, soft lips and similar visible facial arrangement. Lighting and angle differ. No identity, actual age or personality is inferred.

source_levels.boundary: Source registration, search exposure, retained inspiration, native qualification, pixel success and user acceptance remain distinct.

supplemental_observations: Human hand ownership, joint reach, two planted feet and box support are readable.
The camera is lower and the matchbox higher than the authored chest-height/waist-level arrangement; these are authorial fidelity differences.
A small-carriage string is substituted for the specified same locomotive structure across scales.
The matchbox and supporting fingertips provide a visible local familiar-size comparator.
